 1m ago 16.23 EST 64 min: Lyon almost get their third! The ball comes over the top and De Almeida completely mistimes her jump to head it away. She will be relieved that the lurking Katoto, who was through on goal, also mistimes her jump.
 Share 3m ago 16.21 EST 62 min: Arsenal making a triple change to try to salvage this. Hinds, Baum and Cooney-Cross off for Holmberg, Smith and Little.
 Share 5m ago 16.20 EST 60 min: Frustrations quite high now. Baum gets a yellow for a trip on Katoto.
 Share 8m ago 16.17 EST GOAL! Arsenal 0-2 OL Lyonnes (Dumornay 57)
 For all of Arsenal’s efforts in this second half, they concede their second after some poor defending allows Katoto and Chawinga to play off each other and find Dumornay.
 Let that not take away from Dumornay’s clinical finish, whose 16th goal of the season comes after she takes a touch and lashes it into the roof of the net.
 A hill to climb now for the hosts.
 View image in fullscreen Melchie Dumornay pulls the trigger to score Lyon’s second. Photograph: Naomi Baker/Getty Images Share Updated at  16.22 EST 9m ago 16.15 EST 56 min: Foord was in behind for a moment and it is a bit clumsy as she tries to win the ball back from Brand from just outside the box. They both go down and the referee claims it is a free-kick for Lyon, much to Foord’s astonishment. The crowd at Meadow Park start to boo.
 Share 12m ago 16.12 EST 53 min: Russo has a shot blocked as Arsenal start to finally ask Lyon some questions defensively. Against Barcelona, the Gunners were much better in the second half – will this be a repeat?
 Share 14m ago 16.11 EST 50 min: Play is stopped as one of the assistant referees needs a new offside flag. Giráldez is slightly displeased on the touchline, suggesting that she does need the flag and can merely just raise her hand. Unsure of how serious he is being.
 Share 16m ago 16.09 EST 49 min: The best bit of Arsenal attacking play so far in this match as Stanway, Foord and Russo combine to get up the pitch. Maanum then ends up with the ball and her quick pass is misread by Foord, who miscontrols it and allows Grohs to collect.
 Share 18m ago 16.07 EST 47 min: Misa gets low to smother another close-range shot, this time from Chawinga. Lyon have so many dangerous forwards.
 Share 20m ago 16.05 EST Second half: We are back underway! Forty-five minutes for Arsenal to respond? Or will Lyon run away with it?
 Share 33m ago 15.52 EST Half-time reading: 
 Inside women’s football’s difficult rise in Syria: ‘A joy that everyone in the country needed’ Read more Washington Spirit v Kansas City Current: where the NWSL Championship will be won and lost Read more Want your fix of women’s football from the Guardian? Sign up for Moving the Goalposts and get our roundup of women’s football for free twice a week in your inbox.
 Share 37m ago 15.47 EST Half-time: Arsenal 0-1 OL Lyonnes
 Only one minute of added time and the hosts will be happy that those 45 minutes are over. They may only be a goal down but Lyon have outplayed them significantly.
 Share 39m ago 15.46 EST 44 min: Lyon win a corner. Brand takes it but Arsenal manage to A) make sure Renard does not get a clear header; and B) clear the ball.
 Share 40m ago 15.45 EST 43 min: Some tricks and flicks from Lyon as Bacha and Yohannes play with the ball over the top of Fox’s head. The Arsenal defender does not seem too pleased with that. The visitors are happy to waste some time until the half-time whistle.
 Share 42m ago 15.42 EST 40 min: Arsenal finally get out of their own half as they pass the ball around the back. What can they do with their first bit of sustained possession? Fox gets past Bacha but can’t do much against Chawinga. The Arsenal defender and Bacha then get into a bit of a tussle and the referee has to come ease the tensions.
 Share 46m ago 15.39 EST 38 min: Yohannes goes for a curling shot that is just wide off the right post.
 Share 46m ago 15.38 EST 36 min: Good passage of play from Lyon after a slick Yohannes turn. Brand has a go but Hinds with an all-important tackle. She stays down for a few moments but is OK to continue.
 Share 49m ago 15.35 EST 34 min: Lyon fail to clear the ball twice and Russo has a chance to go for goal on the left. She attempts to curl one from just outside the box but her shot is blocked by Egurrola.
 Share 51m ago 15.34 EST 30 min: Lyon win a dangerous free-kick after Foord fouls Bacha on the far left of the pitch. Renard, all 1.87m (6ft 2in) of her, waiting in the box for a good ball in … Only for Brand to hit the side netting. A waste of a chance for Lyon.
 Share 55m ago 15.30 EST 28 min: Huge miss from Katoto! She does the hardest bit so well – controlling the ball over the top by chesting it down in front of her – but the smashes her shot over the bar.
 Share Updated at  15.34 EST 1h ago 15.27 EST GOAL! Arsenal 0-1 OL Lyonnes (Brand 24)
 It is the player that broke Arsenal’s hearts late on in last year’s semi-final and it had been coming. Becho speeds with the ball out wide on the right and her low ball in finds Brand in the middle of the box who hits it first time into the bottom corner.
 Really nice and comfortable finish from the German despite Arsenal having the numbers in the box – not great positioning from De Almeida or Hinds.
 We have a brief VAR check before the restart but nothing in it and the goal stands.
 View image in fullscreen Jule Brand on the mark for OL Lyonnes. Photograph: Julian Finney/UEFA/Getty Images Share Updated at  15.30 EST 1h ago 15.25 EST 23 min: Egurrola gets booked immediately after she comes flying in to tackle Maanum. The Arsenal player stays down for a few moments but she is back on her feet.
 Share 1h ago 15.23 EST 21 min: Misa spills a ball after she comes out to try to catch it. But the Arsenal keeper gets away with it as the ball bounces towards Renard, whose shot is tame and goes wide.
 Share 1h ago 15.20 EST 18 min: Arsenal under real pressure now as they are allowing Lyon a lot of time and space on the ball in the final third. Chawinga has been a handful for Fox.
 Share 1h ago 15.19 EST 16 min: Dumornay has a powerful strike deflected off Stanway and out for a Lyon corner, which Bacha takes but does not amount to much.
 Share 1h ago 15.18 EST 15 min: Looks like Renard headed the ball onto her teammate’s hand. Not a clear obvious error so no calls from VAR for a penalty.
 Share 1h ago 15.17 EST 14 min: Cooney-Cross takes the corner and as the ball lands into the block of players in the box, several Arsenal players call for a handball. VAR will take a look as play continues.
 Share 1h ago 15.16 EST 13 min: Russo’s first chance to break through after some good linkup play. The striker runs off the shoulder of Sangaré but the defender does well to clear it. Arsenal win a corner.
 Share 1h ago 15.14 EST 12 min: Egurrola clips Foord but Arsenal don’t do much with the resulting free-kick. Not much sustained possession from either side so far.
 Share 1h ago 15.11 EST 9 min: Fantastic backheel from Dumornay finds Becho on the right who then goes for goal but Misa gets down quickly to make the save.
 Share Updated at  15.12 EST 1h ago 15.09 EST 7 min: Yohannes with a lovely threaded ball that breaks the lines for Chawinga. It is just a touch too heavy as Misa gets their just in time. A warning for Arsenal.
 Share 1h ago 15.07 EST 5 min: Lyon think they have won a corner but the referee gives it as a goal kick. The visitors respond by pressing the hosts aggressively as they try to build out from the back.
 Share 1h ago 15.06 EST 3 min: Stanway runs into trouble by the name of Katoto, who surges forward and finds Yohannes on the right. The 19-year-old has a bit of space so she has a go for goal but it is off target and does not trouble Misa.
 View image in fullscreen Georgia Stanway loses out to Damaris Egurrola and Marie-Antoinette Katoto. Photograph: Julian Finney/UEFA/Getty Images Share Updated at  15.10 EST 1h ago 15.03 EST 1 min: The teams trading possession in the opening moments. Arsenal will have to be mindful of Lyon’s attacking power in behind.
 Share 1h ago 15.01 EST Kick-off: Arsenal 0-0 OL Lyonnes
 The referee blows the whistle and we are off! Arsenal in their classic red and white and Lyon in all black with some colourful wavy-patterned trim. Here we go!
 Share 1h ago 14.57 EST Meadow Park is in full voice as the teams come out from the tunnel and take to the field.
 Share 2h ago 14.48 EST Chelsea 1-0 PSG: The Blues left it late in their WCL match yesterday with Veerle Buurman’s late scrambling goal the difference at the Cherry Red Records Stadium. Big week for her after her colossal performance against Manchester City, after being subbed on for Kadeisha Buchanan 12 minutes in. Read Suzanne Wrack’s full report below.
 Chelsea go top of WSL as Sandy Baltimore bullet sees off Manchester City Read more Share 2h ago 14.41 EST Exclusive: Fifa is at loggerheads with the UK’s government and four Football Associations over the world governing body’s demands for tax-free status and exemptions from exchange-rate fees at the 2035 Women’s World Cup.
 The UK bid to host the tournament is due to be ratified at an extraordinary Fifa congress in Zurich on Monday, and the Guardian has learned there is tension behind the scenes over many of Fifa’s requirements, which multiple sources involved in the discussions have indicated will not be met.
 Read the full story from Matt Hughes and Tom Garry below.
 Fifa sparks tension with demand for tax-free status in UK for Women’s World Cup Read more Share 2h ago 14.28 EST Lyon: And Jonatan Giráldez’s thoughts are here.
 double quotation mark I think it will be a very difficult match. There is a lot of quality in the opposition squad, a lot of players who can play inside but also attack in behind with quality combinations. In defence too, they are a team capable of handling different high-pressing and block situations. But we played them last season and saw that we were capable of winning. Arsenal are a team that play at the highest level, and tomorrow, of course, we must be at that level if we want to get the three points.
 Share 2h ago 14.18 EST Arsenal: Here is Renée Slegers on the task at hand.
 double quotation mark Lyon is a very aggressive team; they have a lot of fast players, so we’ll have to manage that really well and defend that really well and make sure we’re in good areas on the pitch, and have numbers around the ball.
 We want to play our game. Our ambition is to spend more time on the ball [than we did against Barcelona] and that helps defend as well, because if you’re on the ball you’re automatically not defending!
 I think the closeness, the closeness to the people [at Meadow Park], you feel that, you feel the energy in the stands. You can almost hear what they say and you feel that connection even more. I like that about playing at Meadow Park.
 The challenge is that it’s all very open and close to the opposition, so it’s up to us to find a code language down the sideline maybe! [Laughs] No, we love going there and it’s a special ground for Arsenal Women. That’s where it all started, so it is special that we’re still playing there. Of course, in combination with the Emirates, which really feels like our home as well.
 View image in fullscreen The Gunnersaurus drums up the atmosphere. Photograph: Justin Setterfield/Getty Images Share Updated at  14.56 EST 2h ago 14.12 EST Ones to watch: Alessia Russo will undoubtedly be one of Arsenal’s biggest attacking threats when the sides meet again. The England international has developed an impressive record against Lyon, scoring three goals in five WCL appearances against the French side. Only Marie-Antoinette Katoto, with four, has scored more against them in the competition. Russo has also contributed four goals across her last four meetings with Lyon, with three goals and an assist. Having started the campaign relatively slowly, the striker has rediscovered her prolific touch, most notably with a hat-trick against Benfica that saw her become the all-time leading English goalscorer in WCL history.
 View image in fullscreen Alessia Russo during the Women's Champions League match between Barcelona and Arsenal. Photograph: Alex Burstow/Arsenal FC/Getty Images Caitlin Foord is another Arsenal player who could prove important. The Australian has scored three goals in seven European appearances against Lyon, including a memorable brace during Arsenal’s 5-1 victory in France in October 2022.
 For the visitors, Melchie Dumornay remains a major threat. The Haitian international has already scored four times against Arsenal and has been in excellent form this season, registering 11 goals across all competitions. She also scored twice in Lyon’s 2-1 victory at Meadow Park last season.
 View image in fullscreen Melchie Dumornay wins Player Of The Match award after the Women's Champions League match between Juventus and OL Lyonnes. Photograph: Chris Ricco/UEFA/Getty Images Katoto is another player Arsenal must keep quiet. Her seven goals in this season’s European campaign make her the competition’s leading scorer after four rounds, while Ada Hegerberg’s experience and record of 69 European goals provide Lyon with another attacking option.
 Share 2h ago 14.00 EST Head-to-head record: As mentioned, this will be the 13th meeting between Arsenal and OL Lyonnes , making it the joint-most-played fixture in WCL history, level with Lyon’s encounters against Wolfsburg. The French giants have historically enjoyed the upper hand, winning eight of the previous 12 meetings, with Arsenal recording three victories and one draw. However, the rivalry has become increasingly competitive in recent seasons, with all three of the Gunners’ wins coming since 2022.
 The clubs met three times last season, beginning with a league phase encounter at Meadow Park. Despite Alessia Russo opening the scoring after just seven minutes, a Melchie Dumornay double secured a 2-1 victory for Lyon.
 They were subsequently drawn together in the semi-finals, with Arsenal taking a 2-1 advantage from the first leg thanks to Olivia Smith’s winner. However, Lyon responded in France, claiming a 3-1 victory to progress 4-3 on aggregate. Jule Brand scored in both legs, while Wendie Renard also found the net in the return fixture.
 Interestingly, Arsenal have won just three of their 17 matches against French opposition, with all three victories coming against Lyon. Meanwhile, the French side’s first-ever defeat on a trip to England came against Arsenal in April, ending an impressive 10-game unbeaten away record.
 Share 3h ago 13.50 EST Team news
 Arsenal XI (4-3-3): Misa; Fox, Williamson, De Almeida, Hinds; Stanway, Maanum, Cooney-Cross; Baum, Russo, Ford.
 Lyon XI (4-2-1-3): Grohs; Brand, Sangaré, Renard, Bacha; Egurrola, Yohannes; Dumornay; Becho, Katoto, Chawinga.
 Referee: Silvia Gasperotti (Italy).
 Share Updated at  14.17 EST 3h ago 13.45 EST Preamble
 Two European heavyweights meet tonight as Arsenal welcome OL Lyonnes to Meadow Park for a showdown in the Women’s Champions League. With 10 European titles between them, this is a fixture worthy of a final, but there is plenty at stake as the league phase reaches its closing stages.
 The sides will play their 13th meeting in the competition, making this the joint-most-played fixture in Women’s Champions League history. While Arsenal have enjoyed some recent success against the French giants, Lyon have won seven of their previous 11 encounters and have proved particularly difficult to overcome on English soil.
 Arsenal currently sit fourth in the league phase table, two points behind leaders Lyon, knowing a top-four finish would secure automatic progression to the quarter-finals. However, they face a side in formidable form. Lyon are unbeaten in Europe this season, having scored 20 goals without conceding a single one in their opening four matches.
 As always, send your thoughts, questions, comments, predictions and anything else you want to share to me via email . Kick-off is at 8pm GMT. Team news to come shortly.
